# Todo List

Native port of [beUI Todo List](https://beui.dev/components/agents/todo-list): an agent's plan as a checklist that updates as the agent works.

```tsx
import { TodoList } from "./src";

<TodoList
  title="Implementation plan"
  items={[
    { id: "1", title: "Inspect the data flow", status: "completed" },
    { id: "2", title: "Update the schema", status: "in-progress", progress: 50, detail: "50%" },
    { id: "3", title: "Add coverage", status: "pending" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Behavior

- Each task's mark morphs with its `status`: a dashed ring while `pending`, an arc filling to `progress` while `in-progress` (a spinning arc when there's no progress), a drawn check when `completed` and a cross when `cancelled`.
- Completed titles are struck through left to right.
- The header count rolls as tasks complete. When every task is done, the list icon turns into a green check and the list folds away; it reopens if a task becomes unfinished again. Turn that off with `collapseOnComplete={false}`, or control it with `open`.
- New tasks rise in, and the list scrolls to them once it's taller than `maxHeight` (248 points).

## Accessibility

- Each task reads as its status and title, such as "In progress: Update the schema".
- The header reads as the title and "2 of 4 tasks completed", and reports whether the list is expanded.
- Reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, swaps marks and strikes without drawing and holds the spinner still.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-presence.ts`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `primitives/agent-icons.tsx`, `primitives/disclosure.tsx`, `primitives/rise-in.tsx`, `primitives/roll-text.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`. It uses `react-native-svg` for its marks.

components.readme:
# Tool Approval

Native port of [beUI Tool Approval](https://beui.dev/components/agents/tool-approval): asks before an agent runs a tool, then follows the run to its result.

```tsx
import { ToolApproval, ToolApprovalCode } from "./src";

<ToolApproval
  tool="terminal.run"
  title="Run the test suite?"
  description="The agent wants to run the accessibility tests."
  parameters={[{ id: "command", label: "Command", value: <ToolApprovalCode code="bun test" /> }]}
  status={status}
  result="49 tests passed in 2.1s."
  onApprove={allow}
  onAlwaysAllow={allowAlways}
  onDeny={deny}
/>
```

## Layout

- A quiet top line holds the tool's name and where the run is ("Approval required", "Running", "Completed"), with a matching icon. The status rolls as it changes.
- The title and description span the card. `parameters` sit behind "View details", each label above its value; `ToolApprovalCode` sets commands in monospace.
- "Allow once" spans the card, with "Always allow" (when you pass `onAlwaysAllow`) and "Deny" sharing the row beneath it.

## Behavior

- You move `status` forward: `approving`, `approved`, `running`, then `complete` or `error`; or `denied`. Once you decide, the details fold away and the actions leave.
- While approving or running, a thin bar slides along the card's bottom edge.
- When the run ends, `result` appears in the card: green for `complete`, red for `error`, neutral for `denied`. The card tells the whole story, not just the request.

## Risk

`risk` sets how careful allowing is:

- `low`: a tap allows.
- `normal` (the default): allowing takes a 600 ms press and hold.
- `high`: a 900 ms hold, a red-tinted card and Allow button, and `riskNote` explaining why, such as "Deletes files. This can't be undone."

`confirm` and `holdDuration` override these.

## Better on a phone

- The hold means a stray thumb can't run a tool. A fill sweeps across the button while you hold and drains back if you let go early. The label coaches you: "Keep holding…" while pressed, "Hold to allow" after a tap that let go too soon.
- The actions are full width and 46 points tall, easy to hit with a thumb.
- The card follows the run to its result instead of handing off to another component.

## Accessibility

# Approval Card

Native port of [beUI Approval Card](https://beui.dev/components/agents/approval-card): asks a person to weigh in before an agent continues.

```tsx
import { ApprovalCard } from "./src";

// A few questions, one at a time
<ApprovalCard
  questions={[
    { id: "scope", title: "How focused should the release be?", options, allowCustom: true },
    { id: "checks", title: "Which checks should block publishing?", options: checks, multiple: true },
  ]}
  status={status}
  onSubmit={(answers) => send(answers)}
/>

// Or a review to approve
<ApprovalCard
  title="Publish the update?"
  status={status}
  onApprove={approve}
  onRequestChanges={requestChanges}
  onReject={reject}
>
  {summary}
</ApprovalCard>
```

## Questions

- Single-choice questions use radios and move on 240 ms after a choice, unless `autoAdvance` is false. `multiple` questions use checkboxes.
- `allowCustom` adds a text answer; with no options, the question is free text only. The keyboard's return key moves on.
- Answers and the step are uncontrolled by default; control them with `answers` and `step`.
- After the last question, `onSubmit` gets every answer. Move `status` to `submitting` and then `answered`.

## Review

Without questions, the card shows your `description` and `children`, with Approve and, when you pass their handlers, Request changes and Reject. Move `status` to `approved`, `changes-requested` or `rejected`.

Once decided, the card folds into its status, or your `result` text.

## Better on a phone

- Swipe left for the next question and right for the previous one. A swipe that can't go anywhere, such as past an unanswered question, pulls with resistance and springs back.
- Questions slide in from the side you're heading toward and the old one slides out the other way, so going back feels like going back.
- Long question titles wrap instead of truncating.

## Accessibility

- Options are native radios and checkboxes with their labels and descriptions.
- The progress dots read as "Question 2 of 3".
- Reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, swaps questions and folds without movement.

Copy this directory, `components/button/`, `components/checkbox/`, `components/input/` and `components/radio/` with their files, `hooks/use-presence.ts`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `primitives/agent-icons.tsx`, `primitives/disclosure.tsx`, `primitives/roll-text.tsx`, `primitives/spin-glyph.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`. It uses `react-native-svg` and Gesture Handler.

# Tool Result

Native port of [beUI Tool Result](https://beui.dev/components/agents/tool-result): a tool call's output, streamed in while it runs.

```tsx
import * as Clipboard from "expo-clipboard";
import { ToolResult } from "./src";

<ToolResult
  tool="terminal.run"
  kind="terminal"
  title={running ? "Running tests" : "Tests passed"}
  status={running ? "running" : "success"}
  onCopy={() => Clipboard.setStringAsync(output)}
  onRetry={runAgain}
>
  {output}
</ToolResult>
```

## Behavior

- String output renders in monospace; pass `ToolResultOutput` or any node for more control. `kind` picks the icon: `terminal`, `request` or `custom`.
- It's a card: a header with the kind's icon, the title, the tool name and a note, and a status pill (Running, Completed, Failed, Cancelled) that rolls as it changes.
- Without a `meta` note, the header times the run: it counts up while running and holds the final time, such as "4.1s". Pass `meta` for your own note, such as a status code.
- The output sits in an inset box, tinted red when the run fails. Its footer holds copy and run again, and counts the lines of string output.
- A thin bar slides along the card's bottom edge while it runs.
- It opens when a run starts and folds away when it finishes. Keep it open with `collapseOnComplete={false}`, or control it with `open`.
- Copy (when you pass `onCopy`) shows a check for 1600 ms. Run again appears with `onRetry`.

## Better on a phone

- Output follows the newest line, but stops the moment you drag up to read and picks up again when you return to the end. The web version pulls you back on every line.
- The note and tool name sit on their own line under the title, so a phone-width header never truncates everything at once.

## Accessibility

- The header reads as the title, note, tool and status, and reports whether the output is expanded.
- The output is a polite live region on Android, and the result is marked busy while running.
- Reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, rolls and folds without movement and holds the spinner still.

Copy this directory, `primitives/running-bar.tsx`, `hooks/use-presence.ts`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `primitives/agent-icons.tsx`, `primitives/disclosure.tsx`, `primitives/roll-text.tsx`, `primitives/spin-glyph.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`. It uses `react-native-svg` for its icons.

# Citations

Native port of [beUI Citations](https://beui.dev/components/agents/citations): sources behind an agent's answer, inline and as a list.

```tsx
import { Citation, Citations } from "./src";

<Text>
  Run gestures on the UI thread <Citation item={sources[0]} index={1} />.
</Text>
<Citations citations={sources} defaultOpen />
```

## Parts

- `Citation` is an inline number. Put it inside your text.
- `Citations` is a "Sources" toggle with a count that folds open into the list. Sources rise in as you add them.
- `CitationList` is the list on its own; `CitationStack` shows up to three overlapping favicons; `CitationFavicon` shows one.
- A source has a `title`, an optional `domain` and `url`, and an optional `icon` for things without a favicon, such as files.
- Tapping a source with a `url` opens it with React Native's `Linking`. Pass `onOpenSource` to handle it yourself, such as in an in-app browser.

Favicons load from each site's `/favicon.ico`, the way the web version does, with no third-party service. A globe stands in when a site has none.

## Better on a phone

On the web, a citation number jumps the page down to the source list. On a phone, tapping it springs a card up out of the number with the source's title, domain and an "Open source" button, so you never lose your place in the answer. The card sits above the number when there's room and below it otherwise, and tapping outside closes it.

## Accessibility

- Each number reads as "Citation 2: WAI accessibility patterns". Change it with `label`.
- The toggle reports whether the list is expanded, and rows read as links.
- Reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, opens the card and the list with fades only.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `primitives/agent-icons.tsx`, `primitives/disclosure.tsx`, `primitives/rise-in.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`. It uses `react-native-svg` for its icons.

# Code Block

Native port of [beUI Code Block](https://beui.dev/components/agents/code-block): highlighted code that an agent writes line by line.

```tsx
import * as Clipboard from "expo-clipboard";
import { CodeBlock } from "./src";

<CodeBlock
  code={code}
  filename="summarize.ts"
  language="typescript"
  status={writing ? "streaming" : "complete"}
  highlightLines={[4, 5]}
  onCopy={() => Clipboard.setStringAsync(code)}
/>
```

## Behavior

- Highlighting covers TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript, JSX, JSON, Bash, Python, Swift, Kotlin, Go, Rust, SQL, CSS, YAML and Markdown, in colors that follow light and dark mode. Use `"text"` for none.
- While `status` is `streaming`, the header says "Writing" and the view follows new lines. It says "Ready" once complete.
- `highlightLines` tints whole rows, numbers included. `showLineNumbers` turns the numbers off.
- Copy appears when you pass `onCopy` and shows a check for 1600 ms.

## Better on a phone

- Line numbers stay put while long lines scroll sideways, so you never lose track of which line you're on.
- A button in the header wraps long lines instead, and back. Start wrapped with `wrap`.
- Following stops the moment you drag up to read and resumes when you return to the end.
- Highlighting runs in plain JavaScript as the code arrives, so streamed lines never flash back to plain text.

## Accessibility

- The status is a polite live region, and the block is marked busy while streaming.
- The copy and wrap buttons have names, and wrap reports whether it's on.
- Reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, follows without smooth scrolling and holds the spinner still.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `primitives/agent-icons.tsx`, `primitives/code-tokens.ts`, `primitives/spin-glyph.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`. It uses `react-native-svg` and `prism-react-renderer` for tokenizing.

# File Diff

Native port of [beUI File Diff](https://beui.dev/components/agents/file-diff): a file's changes as an agent applies them.

```tsx
import { FileDiff } from "./src";

<FileDiff
  file="src/runner.ts"
  status={applying ? "streaming" : "complete"}
  lines={[
    { id: "1", oldLine: 18, newLine: 18, content: "export async function runTask() {" },
    { id: "2", type: "removed", oldLine: 19, content: "  return execute(task);" },
    { id: "3", type: "added", newLine: 19, content: "  return normalize(await execute(task));" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Behavior

- Each line is `added`, `removed` or `context` (the default), with old and new line numbers. Added and removed rows are tinted, and the header counts them as they arrive.
- Code is highlighted in `language` (TypeScript by default).
- It opens while changes stream in, follows the newest line, and folds away once `status` is `complete`. Keep it open with `collapseOnComplete={false}`, or control it with `open`.
- Copy appears when you pass `onCopy`.

## Better on a phone

- Long stretches of unchanged lines fold into a row such as "7 unchanged lines", keeping `context` (2) lines beside each change, so a small screen shows the changes rather than the context. Tap the row to see the lines. A stretch at the end isn't folded while changes are still arriving.
- Line numbers and +/− markers stay put while code scrolls sideways.
- Following stops while you drag up to read.

## Accessibility

- The header reads as the file, the counts and whether changes are applied, and reports whether the diff is expanded.
- Each row reads as "Added 19: …", "Removed 19: …" or "Line 18: …".
- Reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, folds without movement and holds the spinner still.

# Image Generation

Native port of [beUI Image Generation](https://beui.dev/components/agents/image-generation): an image coming into being.

```tsx
import { Image } from "react-native";
import { ImageGeneration } from "./src";

<ImageGeneration status={status} prompt="a quiet mountain landscape at sunset">
  <Image source={{ uri }} style={{ width: "100%", height: "100%" }} />
</ImageGeneration>
```

## Behavior

- `status` moves through `queued`, `generating`, `refining` and `complete`, or `error`. You drive it.
- While active, a lattice of dots fills the frame, drawn with Skia. A soft lens wanders across it: dots inside grow, brighten and push outward.
- At `refining` the finished media shows through at 62% under the fading dots. At `complete` it settles into full view and the dots dissolve. The media stays mounted throughout, so nothing shifts.
- The frame reserves `aspectRatio` (1 by default). `size="compact"` caps it at 208 points wide; `"fluid"` fills.
- The status rolls along underneath with a turning glyph, and the `prompt` sits under it in quotes. After an error, `onRetry` adds "Try again".

## Better on a phone

- The web version's lens follows a mouse pointer and is switched off for touch. Here it follows your finger: drag across the placeholder and the lens tracks you, swelling under your touch, then wanders off again when you let go. Turn it off with `interactive={false}`.
- `onLongPress` on the finished image lifts it slightly before firing, ready for a save or share sheet.
- The lens eases at the same speed on 60 Hz and 120 Hz screens.

## Accessibility

- The frame is an image named by `label`, or the status and prompt. The status line is a polite live region, and the frame is marked busy while active.
- Reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, draws one still frame of dots with the lens centered, and swaps statuses without movement.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-presence.ts`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `primitives/agent-icons.tsx`, `primitives/roll-text.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`. It uses `@shopify/react-native-skia`, `react-native-svg` and Gesture Handler.

# Voice Orb

Native port of [beUI Voice Orb](https://beui.dev/components/agents/voice-orb): a grainy liquid sphere that moves with a voice.

```tsx
import { useSharedValue } from "react-native-reanimated";
import { VoiceOrb } from "./src";

const level = useSharedValue(0);
// Feed it your microphone level, 0 to 1, such as from expo-audio metering.

<VoiceOrb activity={level} accessibilityLabel="Listening" onPress={toggleListening} />
```

## Behavior

- `activity` is the voice level from 0 to 1, as a number or a Reanimated shared value. A shared value drives the orb from audio metering without re-rendering. It's smoothed on a fast, critically damped spring.
- Voice opens the folds, ripples the rim and speeds the flow up to 1.6×. The silhouette lifts 2 points, widens 4% and squashes 1.8% at full voice.
- `active={false}` freezes the surface exactly where it is. Time only advances while active, scaled by `speed`.
- `colors` are the base, highlight and shadow as `#RGB` or `#RRGGBB`. `size` defaults to 256 points.
- The surface is the web version's shader, ported to Skia and running on the GPU. Grain and edge softness match the web at up to 2× density.

## Better on a phone

The orb is often the talk button. `onPress` and `onLongPress` make it one: it squishes under your finger like something soft, then springs back.

## Accessibility

- With `accessibilityLabel`, it's an image, or a button when it has `onPress`. Without a label it's hidden from screen readers.
- Reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, draws a still surface with no voice response.

The component never asks for the microphone; your app supplies the level.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`. It uses `@shopify/react-native-skia`.
